scenarios.setup: A car on a circular track with an odometer (distance) and a displacement arrow.

tasks.prompt: Drive the car in a complete circle back to the start. Predict what the Displacement arrow will show.
predictionOptions: Displacement will equal the distance travelled
Displacement will be half the distance
tasks.expectedOutcome: Displacement is zero because the start and end points are the same.
tasks.anomalyExplanation: Distance is a scalar (total path length). Displacement is a vector (change in position). If you return to the start, displacement is zero.

scenarios.setup: An egg, a concrete floor, and a foam cushion.

tasks.prompt: Drop the egg on the concrete. Then drop it on the foam. Predict which one will break.
predictionOptions: The egg on concrete will break
The egg on foam will break
tasks.expectedOutcome: The egg on concrete breaks. The foam increases the time of impact, reducing the force.

tasks.prompt: Both the concrete and foam bring the egg to a stop (change in momentum is the same). Why does the foam protect the egg?
predictionOptions: The foam reduces the egg's momentum
The foam increases the time of impact, reducing the force
tasks.expectedOutcome: The foam increases the time of impact, reducing the force.
tasks.anomalyExplanation: Impulse = Force × Time = Change in Momentum. Since the momentum change is fixed, increasing the time (via foam) decreases the force, keeping the egg intact.

scenarios.setup: A pendulum, a motorized pulley, and a generator.

tasks.prompt: Pull the pendulum back (giving it Potential Energy) and release it. Predict what happens to the energy at the lowest point of the swing.
tasks.expectedOutcome: Kinetic energy is maximum at the lowest point.

tasks.prompt: Attach a generator to the pendulum. Predict what will happen to the swing over time.
predictionOptions: It will stop swinging because the energy is lost
It will stop swinging because the energy is converted to electricity
tasks.expectedOutcome: It will stop swinging because the energy is converted to electricity.
tasks.anomalyExplanation: Energy is never destroyed, only converted (Law of Conservation of Energy). The mechanical energy of the pendulum is converted into electrical energy by the generator.

scenarios.setup: A workstation with a digital balance, stopwatch, graduated cylinder, thermometer, and ammeter.

tasks.prompt: Measure the mass of the block on Earth, then on the Moon (simulated). Predict what changes.
predictionOptions: Mass changes, Weight stays the same
Mass stays the same, Weight changes
tasks.expectedOutcome: Mass stays the same, Weight changes.
tasks.anomalyExplanation: Mass is a fundamental scalar quantity (amount of matter), measured in kg. Weight is a derived vector quantity (Force of gravity = mg), measured in Newtons. Gravity on the Moon is 1/6th of Earth, so weight changes, but mass does not.
